facts.text: Perseverance Rover was deployed at Jezero Crater during Perseverance (Mars 2020) in 2021.

Perseverance landed on 18 February 2021 in Jezero Crater, a 45-km-wide ancient lake bed. Built on Curiosity's proven design but carrying new instruments, its primary mission is to search for signs of ancient microbial life and collect rock samples for future return to Earth. It also carries MOXIE, which demonstrated making oxygen from Martian CO₂.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Found organic molecules in delta sediments and used MOXIE to produce oxygen from Martian CO₂ — a technology critical for future human missions.
Still operational and collecting samples for Mars Sample Return; the most advanced astrobiology laboratory ever sent to another planet.
